item.title: Can Anthropic afford to put safety first?
item.description: The Anthropic IPO raises big questions about the future of AI, the company’s safety-first mission, and how we balance idealism with capitalism. The real story is what happens now — and whether Anthropic can continue to thread the needle of caring about and investing in AI safety while also being a public company beholden to shareholders. We also get into why OpenAI seems happy to have let Anthropic go public first , and why Anthropic’s whole pitch to big customers boils down to the same safety branding that now sits in conflict with the profit-oriented part of its business. Anthropic is the first pure AI lab to go public. Or is OpenAI just retconning the fact that it didn’t go first? Now that Anthropic has gone first and set this historic precedent, OpenAI can ride on its coattails and say, “Yeah, us too.” I doubt they would beat Anthropic’s record.

item.title: Meet Thinking Machines Inkling 2 Mini: 26B Looped MoE Runs on a 32GB Mac
item.description: Thinking Machines Lab has released Inkling 2 Mini , an open-weight looped transformer with 26.4B total parameters. Inkling 2 Mini is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model from Thinking Machines that loops its middle layers. Thinking Machines lists 3 supported setups: 1 NVIDIA DGX Spark, Apple silicon with 32GB+ memory, and other GPUs with 32GB+ VRAM. Serving support covers Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, Ollama, NVIDIA Dynamo and TokenSpeed. A vLLM quick start takes 1 command: vllm serve "thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini" . His most recent endeavor is the launch of an Artificial Intelligence Media Platform, Marktechpost, which stands out for its in-depth coverage of machine learning and deep learning news that is both technically sound and easily understandable by a wide audience.

As per the OpenAI forum announcement , it has powered ChatGPT Plus and Pro voice since October 15. The GPT-Live family replaces the usual cascade of speech-to-text, an LLM and text-to-speech.

item.title: Anthropic mathematician claims to have solved prestigious Millennium Prize problem with Claude
item.description: An Anthropic mathmetician’s latest breakthrough is another sign of how quickly AI is transforming mathematics. Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims he has proved the Riemann hypothesis, one of mathematics’s most notoriously difficult problems, with the help of Claude, cracking a puzzle that has eluded some of the world’s best mathematicians for decades. The Riemann hypothesis is one of seven Millennium Prize problems, which are widely considered some of the most formidable open challenges in mathematics. Anthropic said it was working on the Riemann Hypothesis with Claude in August , but noted at the time: “We don’t expect that the techniques Claude used will lead to proving the Riemann hypothesis.” Alpöge’s solution, presented in Lean, has only been published on his website and has not yet been publicly accepted by the Clay Mathematics Institute, which administers the Millennium Prize and offers a $1 million bounty for each problem solved.

item.title: Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen
item.description: Signal will now restrict screenshots on mobile devices, and says AI agents are ‘hostile to privacy.’ Signal will now restrict screenshots on mobile devices, and says AI agents are ‘hostile to privacy.’ Signal is restricting the ability to take screenshots on Android and iOS devices in an effort to prevent AI agents from reading users’ messages and other data. The agentic AI capabilities built into operating systems that analyze on-screen information to learn more about the user are “undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy,” Signal president Meredith Whittaker said , while urging OS providers to make it easier for app developers to control what data agents can access. “We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy,” Whittaker said.

item.title: Combatting adversarial distillation
item.description: How we’re addressing safety risks of distillation and lessons we’ve learned for strengthening safeguards across the industry. Adversarial distillation creates a path for bad actors to reproduce these capabilities without appropriate safeguards. We’re sharing how OpenAI detects and disrupts adversarial distillation, how we’ve strengthened protections for our models’ protected reasoning, and what we’ve learned that can help strengthen defenses across the industry. We evaluated each student after fine-tuning and again after a lightweight round of reinforcement learning in cybersecurity and coding environments. After reinforcement learning, the exact-trace student still scored higher at the largest inference budget tested on both benchmarks shown, while the summary-trained student scored higher at lower budgets.

item.title: Soket AI Secures $4 Mn as it Rolls Out EKA-1 Model
item.description: Bajaj Finserv's applied research initiative, Finserv Intelligence, has invested approximately $2 million in AI research company Soket AI, with its investee firm Pennant Technologies putting in a further $2 million in the same round. Soket AI, backed by the IndiaAI Mission, has also launched EKA-1, a 26-billion-parameter foundation model under Project EKA, its flagship sovereign AI initiative focused on math, code, and reasoning. The model is being built to support over 100 languages, including Indian and Global South languages, alongside programming languages. The investment supports Soket AI's work on indigenous AI solutions for applications where data security, reliability, and technological sovereignty are critical. He said Soket AI's "efficient reasoning-led models can make advanced AI economically viable for financial services, while allowing us to deploy it securely within our own infrastructure , with full control over data".

item.title: Zerodha Migrates Kite's User Preference Storage From SSDB to Open-Source SQLite-Based System
item.description: Zerodha has built an open-source distributed blob storage system on top of SQLite to handle the large volumes of user interface and workspace data generated by its trading platform Kite. Zerodha uses Blobasaur to store JSON-based preferences for millions of users. The project was developed after the company ran into limitations with its existing storage systems. Zerodha initially used CouchDB before moving to SSDB, a disk-backed database that supported the Redis protocol. Zerodha evaluated several alternatives, including ScyllaDB, PostgreSQL, object storage, and systems designed to distribute files across machines. Explaining one reason for the choice, Chandra wrote, “SQLite is up to 35% faster than raw filesystem I/O.” Blobasaur is written in Rust and uses SQLite to store the data.

item.title: Apple may be developing its own AI agent that runs your Mac
item.description: Apple appears to be working on its own AI agent to conduct computer work on behalf of users — including using apps, accessing websites, and coding, among other things. The news was originally reported by Bloomberg, which spotted a job listing the iPhone maker recently posted for a senior engineering manager to oversee the creation of an “AI agent that can use a computer.” “Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does,” the posting says. “It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple.” The posting additionally notes that the agents should be able to move “fluidly between tools” and “carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs.” TechCrunch reached out to Apple for more information but did not receive a response.

item.title: Anthropic’s 7 founders cashed out nearly $2B in record-breaking IPO
item.description: Anthropic became a public company on Thursday, raising a total of $81.3 billion, including $1.95 billion for its seven founders. That was the midpoint price from Anthropic’s original price range. Anthropic implied in its IPO filings that the founders aren’t entirely in this for the money though. The company points out that these commitments are “voluntary, revocable expressions of each co-founder’s philanthropic intent and do not constitute legally binding obligations.” With the IPO in the record books, there were a few other interesting numbers worth highlighting. $104.8 billion. Just for comparison: When Facebook had its then record-breaking IPO in 2012, it raised $16 billion on IPO day. 28% stake to Amazon and Google combined. As mind-blowing as it is to raise nearly $105 billion, giving Anthropic nearly $230 billion of working capital available (along with capital it already had on hand), the company’s need for future capital is still far greater.

item.title: Hebbia sees improvements in financial research with GPT-6 Astra
item.description: Hebbia sees gains in financial research in tests of GPT‑6 Astra. Hebbia’s Matrix helps bring that research together, linking answers to the documents behind them. Hebbia tested OpenAI’s GPT‑6 Astra to improve two parts of that work: finding the sources a question requires and building a presentation that follows the banker’s brief. In that workflow, GPT‑6 Astra selects documents or Matrix cells to support an answer, then turns the analysis into native PowerPoint slides that follow the user’s structure and guidelines. “Traceability is really important to our users because they’re basing millions of dollars of decisions on what the AI actually comes back with,” Kavita says. “Citations help with traceability as well as giving users confidence that the AI found the right answer.” In Hebbia’s tests, GPT‑6 Astra combined broader source coverage with highly relevant citations.

item.title: Can AI help scientists identify promising drug candidates?
item.description: Introducing MedChemBench, a benchmark that tests how well AI models read molecular structures, interpret experimental results, and choose which compounds to test next. We’re introducing MedChemBench, a benchmark that evaluates AI models on reasoning tasks drawn from medicinal chemistry research. Building AI that can reliably support this work is one step towards helping scientists develop better medicines. For AI to help, it needs to connect changes in molecular structure with experimental evidence and reason about what compounds are worth pursuing. In the illustrated answers, GPT‑5.6 Sol produced a 15-atom ring, while GPT‑5.6 Luna split the molecule into two disconnected fragments. While the benchmark evaluates reasoning from historical evidence rather than real-world drug discovery, its results help identify where models are advancing and where challenges remain.

item.title: These tech outages are giving Y2K, AI agent style
item.description: In the past two weeks, the U.S.’s top businesses have faced technical outages that have disrupted the systems that run everyday life. While there’s no reason to view these outages as cyberattacks, there may be more than coincidence going on: It’s giving AI-native Y2K, frankly. The technical outages are most likely the “growing pains of a security system that’s getting stronger, not weaker,” and that “AI is surfacing vulnerabilities at a speed and scale we’ve never had before through AI tools like Mythos and others,” he told TechCrunch. The thing is, many of these technical flaws have always existed, but because AI is surfacing them so fast, enterprises are rushing to fix them before bad actors can exploit them. “That surge in patching is disrupting things in the short term,” he said. This was, perhaps, the first moment when legacy meets modern, Anusha Iyer, a software engineer and founder of the security startup Corsha, told TechCrunch.

item.title: Meta’s Muse Charm might cost $300
item.description: The Information has reported a potential price for the Muse Charm, which is likely to ship in time for the holidays. The Information has reported a potential price for the Muse Charm, which is likely to ship in time for the holidays. Meta is planning to price the Muse Charm, a little gadget with a screen that lets you chat with your Muse AI agent, at $300, based on The Information . It has a fingerprint sensor, and you can tap it to be able to talk to a Muse AI agent without unlocking a phone or opening an app. The company is also working on a smartwatch, The Information says, but a launch for that has been pushed to 2027 as Meta tries to get Muse Charm out the door. Meta also open sourced code to let users make their own Muse gadgets , which my colleague Sean Hollister used to make his own DIY Muse Charm .

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO could deliver $156B to charity
item.description: Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO has made quite a few people generationally wealthy, but it will also be an enormous windfall for the causes backed by the frontier lab and its employees. As you might expect from a company whose leadership emerged from the world of effective altruism (EA), Anthropic has multiple different avenues for cash raised in its market debut to be directed to philanthropy. First, the company’s Public Benefit Fund, or PBF (analogous to OpenAI’s foundation), was allotted 5% of the company’s shares, almost 850 million. The PBF’s money will be focused on research and activities related to increasing the benefit of artificial intelligence to humanity. Anthropic also donated $50 million to the city of San Francisco last week. And it seems likely that significant funding will be allocated to AI safety research, given the concerns expressed about that subject by many Anthropic employees.

item.title: Google gives Gemini the ability to use your Mac for you
item.description: Google on Thursday revealed that it is bringing computer use to its Gemini desktop application on macOS, allowing its AI to complete tasks on users’ behalf, navigating native Mac apps, and browsing websites in the background. The tech giant is a little late to the game with this launch, as other leading AI model makers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta have already been offering agentic features in their desktop applications for some time. Meanwhile, Google only this week revealed the broader rollout of Gemini’s “Tasks,” the in-app feature that allows the AI to work more as an agent, helping users sign into websites, make online purchases, or book appointments. Google also only recently began admitting early testers to try its revamped “CC” AI agent, revealed in September , which is designed to help families stay organized across email, calendars, chats, and tasks.
